faq.a: No, and the tool states this plainly. It uses classical interpolation, not AI super-resolution, so it can't invent detail that was never captured — it makes images larger and sharper-looking, not genuinely higher-resolution. For true detail reconstruction you'd need a dedicated AI upscaler; for documents or IDs, don't trust detail that only appears after upscaling.

faq.q: What upscaling algorithms can I choose?
faq.a: Four: Browser Bicubic (fast high-quality smoothing), Stepwise (repeated ~1.8x jumps to preserve edge detail), Lanczos-style resampling (a sinc-windowed resample computed on pixel data — sharpest for photos but slower), and Nearest-Neighbour (no blending, ideal for pixel art). Scale options are 2x, 3x, 4x, 8x or a custom target size with optional aspect lock.

After upscaling you can apply an unsharp mask (adjustable amount up to 200% and radius up to 5px), noise reduction via a median filter (0–3 passes), contrast (−50 to +50) and saturation (0–200%). Output can be PNG, JPEG or WebP with a quality slider for the lossy formats. A before/after slider and 100% side-by-side view let you judge the result.

faq.q: Can it upscale several images together?
faq.a: Yes. Drop multiple images and navigate between them with Prev/Next; 'Process All & Download ZIP' applies the current settings to every image with a progress bar and bundles them into a ZIP. Best results come from clean source images at moderate enlargement — heavily compressed JPEGs and already-blurry photos enlarge their artefacts rather than improving.
